papers.title: Behavioral Compositionality of Sparse Autoencoder Representations
papers.problem: Explaining AI features one by one misses how features act together.
papers.fix: Pairs of features predict AI behavior much better; steering ranking accuracy rises from 0.5874 to 0.7790.
papers.practicalUseCase: Single-feature explanations of an AI model can mislead you, so test feature pairs before trusting a claim.
papers.limitation: The tests cover 18 model and behavior settings, so results may differ for other models.

papers.title: Diminishing Returns of Data in Sparse Autoencoders: Functional Behavior does not Guarantee Feature Reproducibility
papers.problem: Teams train interpretation tools for AI on huge data piles, and nobody knew how much data they need.
papers.fix: Small data rebuilds the signal well, but matched features rise only from 2% at 5M tokens to 29% at 50M.
papers.practicalUseCase: Use small data budgets for cheap tools, but check that features repeat before you trust them.
papers.limitation: Tests used four tool designs on three language models, so other setups may differ.

papers.title: LEASH: Uncertainty-Aware Weak-to-Strong Escalation and Oversight for Computer-Use Agents
papers.problem: Small AI agents that run your computer fail often, and big models cost too much at every step.
papers.fix: LEASH calls the big model only if the small one seems unsure, matching Claude Opus 5 at 73.66% with 19.2% less cost.
papers.practicalUseCase: You can cut agent costs by calling the strong model only on risky steps.
papers.limitation: Results come from one benchmark, OSWorld, so real tasks may behave differently.

papers.title: Scalable Weak-to-Strong Verifier Hardening for Agent Environments
papers.problem: Agents can cheat the scripts that grade their work and earn full credit without doing the task.
papers.fix: A loop where one agent attacks the grader and another repairs it cut cheating across Terminal Bench, KernelBench, and SETA.
papers.practicalUseCase: Run an automatic attack-and-repair loop on your agent graders before you trust their scores.
papers.limitation: It tested only three environments and cannot prove that future stronger models will find no new cheats.

papers.title: LeanPRM: Lean-Grounded Process Supervision for Natural Language Proof Verification
papers.problem: Checking AI-written math proofs step by step is slow, because step labels need human experts.
papers.fix: Lean labeled 152K steps in 10,634 proofs without humans, lifting a small verifier's accuracy from 48.2 to 74.7.
papers.practicalUseCase: Machine-made labels can replace human annotators, so verifiers for hard AI output get cheaper to build.
papers.limitation: The accuracy test used only 200 proofs, and Lean labels need formal statements to exist.

papers.title: Sustainability Committees and Environmental Initiatives: Insights from Dual Banking Systems in Emerging Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Banks in emerging markets set up sustainability committees, but nobody knew if those committees change green results.
papers.fix: Banks with a sustainability committee score higher on green results, but Islamic banks gain only on overall and resource-saving scores.
papers.practicalUseCase: Judge a bank's green claims by its products and innovations, not by whether it has a committee.
papers.limitation: It shows links in panel data, not cause, and covers only emerging-market banks.

papers.title: Trends and Determinants of Sustainability Sukuk Issuance: Evidence from Global Markets
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Little was known about why sustainability sukuk issuance grows slowly and stays concentrated in a few countries.
papers.fix: Across 11,944 sukuk issues, equity-based contracts, strong security, and USD or Euro currency give larger issues.
papers.practicalUseCase: Issuers who want bigger sustainability sukuk should use equity-based contracts and major currencies, and policymakers should cut second-party opinion costs.
papers.limitation: Data ends in 2022 and shows links between features and size, not cause.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence and Big Data Strategies to Enhance Islamic Banks’ Competitiveness and Sustainable Development
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Islamic banks in Jordan lacked proof that AI and big data actually help them compete.
papers.fix: In a survey of 214 managers, AI, data analytics, and data management all link to better competitiveness and sustainable development.
papers.practicalUseCase: Islamic banks should invest in AI and data systems first, since staff digital skill helped competitiveness only.
papers.limitation: It surveyed managers in Jordan at one point in time, so it cannot prove cause.

papers.title: ICT, High-Tech Exports, and Institutions as Drivers of Bank Expansion Growth in a Dual Banking System
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.problem: Researchers did not know what drives growth in banks that run both Islamic and conventional systems.
papers.fix: Across 218 banks in 12 countries, ICT adoption drives growth most, and high-tech exports help only when paired with ICT.
papers.practicalUseCase: Banks that want growth should fund digital systems first, and governments should build strong institutions around them.
papers.limitation: It covers 218 banks in 12 countries from 2010 to 2023, so other markets may differ.

papers.title: Determinants of Financial Inclusion in the OIC and OECD Countries: Are They Different?
papers.venue: Journal of Islamic Monetary Economics and Finance
papers.institution: International Centre for Education in Islamic Finance
papers.problem: Muslim-majority countries still leave many people outside formal finance, despite fast growth in Islamic finance.
papers.fix: In OIC countries, income, tertiary education, institution quality, and internet access drive financial inclusion more than in OECD countries.
papers.practicalUseCase: Policymakers in OIC countries should invest in digital infrastructure, youth and women, and income growth to bring people into banking.
papers.limitation: It covers only 35 countries from 2005 to 2021, so results may not fit every country.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Doctoral students get powerful AI tools, yet some produce innovative research and others do not.
papers.fix: Both inner drive and outside pressure raise innovation together, and AI skill with good resources strengthens the effect.
papers.practicalUseCase: Build your AI skill and secure research support, since good resources can make up for weak motivation.
papers.limitation: It used one self-reported survey at a single time, so it cannot prove cause and effect.
